Nothing changes until the server restarts. If the dashboard’s address is wrong you will not be able to reach this page after that, and the way back is a shell on the host and \"teanode-server config\".

Restart %1$s? Mail will not be accepted for a few seconds.
The process exits and whatever started it is expected to start a new one. Mail already accepted is on disk and is delivered afterwards; a sender connecting during those few seconds will try again.
Nothing has changed that a restart would pick up.
Changed since this instance started, and not in use yet: %1$s. Restarting picks them up.

The release is downloaded and checked against the checksums published with it, and this server then restarts into it. That takes a few seconds during which mail is not accepted; senders retry. The binary it replaces is kept, so going back does not need the network.
Download and restart
Upgrade this server to %1$s?
Automatic upgrades are on: a new release is installed without being asked.
Automatic upgrades are on, between %1$s local time: a new release is installed without being asked.
Checking for releases is turned off (upgrade.enabled), so this says what was known when it was last on.

Where mail and state are written. Shown and not editable here: a server restarted against a different directory does not find what is in the old one, and the mail simply is not there any more. Moving it is done with the server stopped.
